thesis: This episode argues that Auto1 has finally achieved EBITDA profitability in 2024 after 12 years of losses, demonstrating that the business model works at scale. It highlights the company's ability to arbitrage regional price differences and leverage centralized refurbishment centers for cheaper procurement, while noting that CEO Christian Berteman has significant upside incentives tied to share price and EBITDA targets by 2030.

claims.claim: The company achieved EBITDA profitability in 2024 after 12 years of losses, proving the economics can work at scale.
claims.quote: the other key competitive milestone for the business was in 2024, really their only competitor called Kazoo collapsed after they'd raised more than two billion euros. I also don't think it's a coincidence that in 2024 auto-1 reached its first year of EBITDA profitability.

claims.claim: CEO Christian Berteman has a long-term incentive plan with significant upside if he hits share price and EBITDA targets by 2030.
